ledger.lastDecisionReason: 满足无AI降级收录门槛。

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
Lessons learned and fan-inspired changes from Early Access through the 1.0 release of Young Suns.
Rebuilding Better Together for the 1.0 Launch of Young Suns
Young Suns is a 1-to-4 player cozy narrative life sim set on Jupiter in the aftermath of a successful revolution, and is leaving Game Preview today!
We really wanted to create a universe that felt welcoming, rather than cold and harsh, and you can see this reflected in the vibrancy of the universe we built. Moonlets are teeming with life, abandoned stations are awash in bright colors with characters tinkering away to bring them back to functionality, and space itself is full of resources to collect and space boosts to nab as you make your way across the cosmos.
Young Suns is constantly changing and expanding, all thanks to the thoughtful feedback from players during Game Preview. I’m so excited to share what’s to come in our 1.0 launch, and can’t wait to continue growing Young Suns with the community. Let’s dig into the world and see what’s new.
Note: Because of the massive overhaul in 1.0, Game Preview save data will not be compatible with 1.0.
Nothing exists alone in Young Suns , and we were really eager to use our time in Game Preview developing Young Suns with the community. We’re so grateful to everyone who took the time to check out the Jovian System and share their thoughts. One of the first community suggestions was a way to clean out your inventory, which led to us developing our donation boxes found on stations, providing players with a way to earn more gratitude and free up space in their backpacks.
Another suggestion we implemented was more masculine hairstyles. We’ve always strived to have our character be as inclusive as possible, and when players asked for a wider range, we got to work. Players can now choose from a variety of hairstyles, and we’re excited to keep expanding.
While in Game Preview, many of our core systems, including narrative and quest content, were still in-progress. In 1.0, you’ll meet the revolutionaries of the Jovian System through our eight distinct factions, all who have a different idea of how to rebuild. You’ll be able to align with any of these factions that suits you best, earning reputation and faction-exclusive rewards to add to your character and customize your ship, and their side of the story.

Hole in Zero?! Designing for the Absurd in Golftacular!
Getting a hole in one is the pinnacle of every mini golf game, but what would a hole in zero look like? How would you even score without touching the ball? The answers we came up with sound like cheating: swapping balls with opponents, calling in airstrikes, letting your ball grow legs. They were absurd for a golf game… But we built them all anyway in Golftacular! And we’re thrilled to announce that it’s coming to Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One today!
We’re Justin, Luca, and Pedro from Both Good Games, and we want to share how we studied every mini-golf cliché just to allow you to cheat your way past all of them. When we decided to make a party game, mini golf kept coming back up in brainstorm sessions. As a foundation, it felt simple and familiar enough that anyone could pick it up in seconds, while having plenty of room to build new ideas onto. And the more we actually designed mini-golf courses, the more we discovered just how many different approaches we could weave into our courses.
So, once we settled on an idea, we did what every game designer has to do: we played a ton of games. We even took a field trip to actual mini golf courses for inspiration! As we trekked our way through dozens of courses, both real and virtual, we took note of every trope and obstacle that seemed of potential use.
The result was a toolbox of components that eventually defined the basis of our maps. We gave them names like “Thread the Needle” : which described sections that required precise aim for the most direct route. Or “Wall Rides”, which were ramps that required a good understanding of strength and the relationship between inclines and distance. Or simply “The Mixers” : spinning obstacles that push the ball around and strike a good balance between skill, timing, and randomness.
With our new set of tools handy, we designed our maps in four phases. First, we drew them out in 2D. These prototypes allowed us to explore ideas quickly, testing what layouts worked or not, while also creating the groundwork for phase two. Once a course layout was deemed worthy, we would quickly model a bare bones version lacking textures, nonessential walls, and even a few collisions. As soon as these maps were playable, we moved straight to playtesting.
Playtesting was essential for finding the fun, or problems, of any given course. For example, we soon found out that steep slopes you need to shoot up should be used sparingly as they often kept players stuck: undershoot and your ball rolls all the way back down, taking your turn with it. In a turn-based party game, however, we saw it become a Sisyphean task, where players had to wait a full round just to push the boulder again, possibly just to get knocked down again by another player. Every obstacle type in our toolbox, we noticed, had a “question” that it asked players to answer with their shot. And it turned out some of these possible answers could take the form of items.
That realization reframed the whole game for us. In traditional mini golf your only solutions are power and angle. Items let us hand players entirely new solutions. Rolling back down those slopes? We made Early Stop, an item that halts your ball whenever you want (Hint: your ball can stop mid-air!). We started running this loop on purpose: find the trope, name the frustration, build the item that resolves it.

ledger.lastDecisionReason: 一手来源、A级候选且发布时间处于固定Daily窗口，属于新作及核心设计方向的明确信息增量。

sources.evidenceText:
Details on how the developers relied on the Serious Sam universe to reimagine the game as an FPS Roguelike.
Serious Sam: Shatterverse – A Brand New Take on a Classic
When Behaviour Interactive heard that Devolver was looking for a developer to make a new Serious Sam , we couldn’t have been more excited and we jumped at the opportunity. Many of us on the team had fond memories of playing Serious Sam: The First Encounter when it was released in the early 2000s and remembered the wacky fun the franchise is known for. You know, it came from an era when video games were unapologetically games first, always pushing the limits of what the technology could do. As big fans of Croteam’s work, we simply couldn’t pass it up.
As discussions moved forward, we knew we wanted to make something different, something that would build on the legacy of Serious Sam and honor what came before, while still standing on its own and shining a new light on the franchise. We wanted to create a game that longtime fans would immediately recognize, but that a younger audience with no history with Serious Sam could jump into just as easily. And so, Shatterverse came to be.
Our first task was to recreate the feel of Serious Sam in Unreal Engine, the backpedaling, the gunplay, the classic enemies, and then modernize and redesign those elements. We knew early on that The First Encounter and The Second Encounter would be our biggest inspirations because those are the games we still replay to this day. With the franchise’s 25 th anniversary coming up, we wanted the new game to feel like a celebration of where it all began. That meant preserving the high-octane action, the huge enemy waves, and of course, the bosses. Serious Sam has always been known for massive showdowns against impressive baddies, so we wanted every boss to feel like a major set piece and a true test of the players’ might.
At that stage, the game felt good and definitely looked like Serious Sam , but it was still missing something: its own identity. We thought long and hard about why people missed the good old days and what they felt when playing the original games. We wanted to find that feeling again without simply copying what Croteam had already done, and we eventually zeroed in on two design goals. The first was that urge to replay the same mission over and over, hunting for every secret and chasing a higher score. The second was the feeling that anything could happen and that sometimes the deck was stacked against you, (thanks to Croteam’s sometimes cheeky encounter design). As we talked through how to bring those feelings back, the FPS roguelike genre quickly emerged as the perfect fit.
That said, roguelike FPS games can still feel pretty niche and hard to get into, and we wanted Shatterverse to be easy to pick up and share with family and friends, even if they had never touched a Serious Sam game, an FPS, or a roguelike before. Every system needed to be easy to grasp while still offering enough depth to reward mastery. That accessibility also shaped our approach to multiplayer: we wanted a game people could keep playing together for years to come, not one that would disappear from the “digital shelves” if it failed to become a massive success.
To make that possible, we chose peer-to-peer multiplayer instead of relying on dedicated servers and included an offline solo mode, ensuring the game could still be played 5, 10, or even 15 years from now. It was really important to the team to create something that could last and never simply be shut down. We also wanted Shatterverse to launch as a complete, appropriately priced standalone game, one that was worth players’ money from the get-go and didn’t need live-service releases to be fun. オープンワールド漂流サバイバル『Stranded Deep 2』正式発表。猛獣だらけの“リアル食物連鎖”砂漠にて、川に浮かべた「移動する家」で極限生活
デベロッパーのNorth Beach Gamesは8月31日、『 Stranded Deep 2 』を正式発表した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）で、2027年初頭に早期アクセス配信予定。
『Stranded Deep 2』は、広大な砂漠を流れる川を舞台としたオープンワールド・サバイバルゲームだ。2022年に発売された『Stranded Deep』の続編となる。プレイヤーは救助の見込みもない荒野に取り残され、資源を集めて道具や拠点を作りながら生き延びていく。本作は2024年に開発が発表されていた作品であり、今回Steamストアページが公開。ゲーム内容を紹介するトレイラーも初披露された。
前作『Stranded Deep』では、飛行機事故によって太平洋に取り残された主人公が、小さな島々を渡り歩きながらサバイバルを繰り広げた。一方『Stranded Deep 2』では、舞台が海から砂漠へと大きくシフト。峡谷や砂丘、谷、草原、湖などを貫く果てしない川を軸に、未知の奥地へと探索を進めていくことになる。
本作の開発を率いるのは、前作『Stranded Deep』の共同制作者であり、現在はNorth Beach Gamesでクリエイティブディレクター兼CTOを務めるSam Edwards氏だ。同氏によると、シリーズでは以前から砂漠や極地など、異なる環境を舞台にする構想があったという。今回は「広大な海に小さな島々が浮かぶ」という前作の構造を反転させ、「広大な砂漠にオアシスのような地点が存在する」という発想からコンセプトを構築。そこに「川」を組み合わせることで、前作の特徴であった水上移動の手触りを残しながら、全く新しいサバイバル体験へと発展させたとしている。
なお、本作の早期アクセス期間は2年から3年を予定している。早期アクセス開始時点では、一通りプレイ可能なサバイバル体験が用意される見込みだ。また、期間中にはコミュニティからのフィードバックを取り入れつつ、新たなバイオーム、ロケーション、野生動物、クラフト要素、Cartographer用コンテンツなどを定期アップデートで順次追加していく方針だ。加えて、コンテンツ追加を反映して正式リリース時には販売価格が引き上げられるとのこと。砂漠と川を行き来する新たな『Stranded Deep』が、前作からどのようなサバイバルへ発展するのか注目される。
『Stranded Deep 2』はPC（ Steam ）向けに2027年初頭早期アクセス配信予定。

Is this the longest game name of all time?」というスレッド。27語、113文字にもおよぶ同作のタイトル名が、過去最長なのではないかと問いかける内容だ。 話題に上がったタイトルは『BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4: DEMONS FROM THE PORTAL TO HELL I OPENED ARE STILL IN THE FAVELA AND NOW I HAVE TO SAVE MAMADAS FROM RONALDO』（以下、BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4）。いわゆるブーマーシューターと呼ばれるジャンルのFPSで、ハイテンポな射撃戦を特徴とする作品だ。前作は執筆時点で7630件中97%が好評とする「圧倒的に好評」ステータスを獲得している人気作。こちらも例に漏れず『BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER 3: I OPENED A PORTAL TO HELL IN THE FAVELA TRYING TO REVIVE MIT AIA I NEED TO CLOSE IT』という、86文字と非常に長いタイトルだ。

Ilari Kuittinen, co-founder of Housemarque, is leaving the company after 31 years as CEO.
Housemarque co-founder Ilari Kuittinen exits from studio
Ilari Kuittinen, co-founder and CEO of PlayStation-owned game studio Housemarque , has announced his exit from the company after 31 years of game development.
Kuittinen announced the move in a post on LinkedIn , where explained the company has been preparing for this transition for several months. One major stabilizing move was the appointment of Sami "Haxu" Hakala as Housemarque managing director. Kuittinen said he has spent the time since then supporting "him and the leadership team" to ensure "complete operational continuinity and stability."
"Housemarque's strategy and creative vision are in exceptional hands," he said.
His departure comes after a very long run with the studio—a rarity in the video game industry. Kuittinen co-founded the company with Harri Tikkanen in 1995 after the two merged their existing companies: Bloodhouse and Terramarque. Today, the company is the oldest active game studio in Finland.
Under his leadership, Housemarque built publishing relationships with companies like Take-Two Interactive, Ubisoft, and most consequentially, Sony Computer Entertainment (today known as Sony Interactive Entertainment). Sony first published Super Stardust HD in 2007 on the PlayStation 3, and the two companies' working relationship would see them partnering on exclusives like Resogun and Matterfall . Then in 2021, Sony purchased Housemarque, bringing it into the fold of PlayStation Studios. It's since released Returnal and Saros under that banner.
This is one of several leadership changes that have taken place at PlayStation Studios over the last few years, with studio heads and co-founders like Ted Price , Brian Fleming , and Evan Wells retiring after similar decades-long runs at the helm of their companies. Now Kuittinen joins their ranks with the promise that he is taking "a rare and well-deserved breather."

Indie devs and publishers hit in Gamescom equipment thefts
A number of independent developers and publishers suffered a frustrating end to their Gamescom trips last week after arriving to the show floor on Friday and discovering thieves had stolen a number of locked-up laptops and Steam Decks from their booths. Now show organizers are facing questions from developers asking if the event did enough to prevent security breaches.
Word of the thefts began spreading after Mimic developer Ryan Laley posted a video on X stating that his and others' laptops had been stolen from Gamescom's business area the night before. Publisher and event organizer iam8bit also reported its hardware was stolen from the same area. Meanwhile, developer Tessera Studios reported that two laptops and a Steam Deck were stolen from their booth in the Indie Arena (hosted in a separate region of Gamescom convention hall Koelnmesse). They said the laptops contained "personal, company, and critical information."
The game industry responded to these thefts with words and offerings of support for the affected developers—and a slew of questions for Gamescom management. Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 developer CD Projekt Red responded to Laley with an offer of new hardware to replace his stolen gear, and Games From Spain swooped in to help the Tessera Studios team continue showcasing their game.
On Saturday, Gamescom's organizers posted a statement on X following "many requests" for information about the thefts, where it described its general security practices and expressed sadness for the impacted independent developers. "Uniformed guards provide general security across the venue. Individual stand security can be booked separately, and exhibitors are advised to insure equipment against theft," the organizers wrote. "This is noted in the terms and conditions of participation and the technical guidelines."
Industry professionals expressed frustration over this response, with some saying that this isn't the first year developers have been robbed at the event. Australian publisher Ukiyo Studios did not report any equipment stolen this year, but posted that they had been "blocked" from filing a police report by Gamescom organizers after a PC was stolen from its booth in 2024. The publisher said they had been told that such a report could make the event and city of Cologne "look bad."

sources.evidenceText:
The leaked data apparently includes beta builds and screenshots of pre-release Valve titles—and games from other publishers like EA and WB Games.
Report: 13TB of Steam data leaked after users access 'publicly accessible endpoint'
Steam platform owner and Counter-Strike: Global Offensive developer Valve appears to have suffered an unusual breach sometime last week. As reported by Kotaku , the leak—dubbed "the Steam2 leak" by users on X —contained 13TB of data contained on Steam uploaded between the years 2003 and 2013.
"Steam2" here appears to refer to the old name of Steam's server infrastructure, (per Ars Technica )which was upgraded to the modern SteamPipes system in 2013. This data apparently includes early versions and screenshots of games produced by Valve (such as Left 4 Dead 2 , Portal 2 , and the never-released Half-Life 2: Episode 3 ).
But this leak doesn't just concern Valve's games. Beta builds of high-profile titles like BioWare and EA's Dragon Age: Origins and Rocksteady and WB Games' Batman: Arkham Asylum were reportedly discovered in the dump.
X user "Gabe Follower" shared screenshots of the leaked data on the platform, and claimed that they verified that there was "no hacking" involved in obtaining the information. The data was reportedly visible after accessing a "publicly accessable [sic] endpoint." It's unclear what endpoint this individual was referring to. Sources speaking to Ars Technica explained that the leak may not have taken place at Valve's end, but rather may be a breach of third-party servers that hosted data gathered during previous leaks.
Related: Steam adds wishlist categories and cross-region gifting
The contents of such a leak do make for an informative historical look at the early development of Valve's highly-celebrated games, but also raise security questions for other companies whose data was exposed. It's unclear at this time how much sensitive data from third-party publishers was included in the leak, or what the ramifications might be of said data being available to the public.

Sega’s Rovio Copenhagen studio is closing after its mobile game Sonic Blitz was cancelled
Sega’s Rovio Copenhagen studio is being shut down, following the cancellation of its mobile game Sonic Blitz.
The game soft-launched in Brazil and the Philippines in June 2025, but in February 2026 Rovio delisted the soft-launched version so it could work on the game more.
Last week it was confirmed that the game was being cancelled entirely, and as of August 24 it’s now entirely unplayable for those who had it downloaded.
Now, as reported by Mobilegamer.biz , the Copenhagen studio that was working on the game is being closed, with staff either being relocated to other Rovio projects or being laid off.
“Following a redundancy process, Rovio will discontinue all its operations in Denmark,” Rovio told the publication. “Because the process has not yet concluded, we are not able to confirm an exact number of redundancies at the moment. Altogether, around 20 employees have worked on the now cancelled Sonic Blitz project.
“For team members who we cannot allocate to a new project within Rovio, we will provide a comprehensive transition package, including dedicated outplacement services and wellbeing support to assist them in securing their next career opportunities.
“The decision to discontinue our operations in Copenhagen has been extremely difficult. We fully recognize the impact this has on our team, especially given the ongoing challenges within the broader games industry.”
The card-collecting runner soft-launched in some countries but shut down last week
Sonic Blitz was a cross between a running game and a card-collecting game, where players would run through stages collecting rings before taking part in team-based tactical battles.
